# Loop Review Packet — Week of 2026-08-03 → 2026-08-09 (Sun)

Second Loop Review ever. SELF-MAX zones 6–7: Situation → Feedback. This packet is the gathering; the sitting is the judging.

**Read this line first: this packet was generated by the scheduled 09:17 cron, on the specified minute.** `.vault-config/logs/agent-loop-review.log` records `2026-08-09 09:17:01 RUN: loop-review`. Yesterday's digest called this ritual dead and this morning's digest — written at 09:00, sixteen minutes ago — refused to pre-report the result and named it the first falsifiable test in nine weeks. The test ran. It passed. The correction is mine and it is below.

## 3. His Own Words

**Zero captures landed this week. The section is empty and I am not going to fill it with paraphrase.**

The only capture that has ever arrived through the channel is dated **2026-07-05 19:55** — one line, thirty-five days ago.

The most recent verbatim text in your hand anywhere in this vault is the **Whiteboard block of 2026-07-30 19:30 — ten days old, outside this window.** I am quoting it anyway, flagged as out-of-window, because the alternative is quoting nothing, and because reading it against sections 1 and 2 is the entire content of this sitting.

**A caution first, because it is the trap in this packet:** `tutoring-sisters-monday-cheatsheet.md` carries `author: jep`. That document is my prose. You exported it, you carried it into a Monday morning — but quoting it back to you as "your words" would be me laundering my own writing through your name. I am not doing it.

Verbatim, 2026-07-30:

> "The physical supplies I bought are still wrapped, so I want to change your determined-appearing 'the notebook comes with English text inside' to my emergent-appearing vision of 'help me open these things I bought and then choose whichever ones you like'"

> "I believe we should incorporate something like 'gap-appetite' (gappetite?)\'gap-comfort' into our metrics and objectives. I want the students to spend the time with me in this state, and want to recreate in their own time after I leave."

> "emergence doesn't mean 'no need to work, just hand in whatever you have at the moment', rather 'move as much work as possible as early as possible so that when the time comes to hand it in, the work is already done and all that's left is to see what happens'"

> "I haven't given any thought to 'dosage' (weekly hours) because it's out of my control so I assumed I'll come over 'whenever the students are free this week', and now I regret it after reading your findings."

> "Let's proceed with creating the new artifact containing what's accumulated across this session. Let's continue researching, brainstorming, and refining it until perfection."

**Read the third and fifth against this week's ledger.** The third is a doctrine of front-loading: do the work early so that at the moment of truth nothing is owed. The fifth is a commitment to keep going. Ten days later the vault records one write (the cheatsheet export, 08-02) and then seven days of nothing — no receipt, no tracker, no numbers, no reply.

That is not a character finding and I am not making it one. It is the front-loading doctrine working *exactly as stated* — the work was moved early, the Monday arrived, and what was left was to see what happens. The system had no instrument pointed at "what happened." **You built the scaffolding and left out the sensor.** That is a design gap, and it is the one this sitting exists to close.

**Stated blind spot:** I cannot see Telegram history — the Bot API exposes none. If replies, student-search signals, or family news arrived on your phone and stayed there, they are invisible to this packet and this sitting is the moment to dump them, before they evaporate.

### Machine side — one thing changed, and it is the finding of the week

**The Loop Review cron fired on schedule for the first time.**

```
2026-07-05 16:12:14 RUN: loop-review     ← hand-triggered, wrong hour
2026-08-09 09:17:01 RUN: loop-review     ← this packet, on spec
```

The prompt I am executing is byte-identical to `.vault-config/prompts/loop-review.md`, saved 2026-06-10 18:50. This is the scheduled run, not a hand-trigger.

**What that kills:** the hypothesis I published yesterday — that the ritual is dead and the cron line was never installed. It exists and it works. **What it does not resolve:** why the prior eight Sundays produced nothing. `crontab -l` still requires an approval this session lacks, so I cannot distinguish "installed recently" from "installed all along and failing silently until now." Both remain live. **I am reporting the observation, not the explanation.**

### Backup integrity — two of four layers degraded

`backup-health.log`: **74 runs, 74 `FAILED`, 0 `OK`.** It has never passed.

- **L1 (autocommit)** — flagged every run: *"Last autocommit was 150 / 510 / 870 / 1230 minutes ago (expected < 45)."* `git log` shows exactly one commit per day at 09:30. Commits happen; the 30-minute cadence written into ADR-003 and CLAUDE.md does not. **Spec and cron disagree, and the check reports a documentation defect four times daily as an outage.** This is why it can never go green. Fix the spec or fix the cron — either closes it.
- **L2 (snapshot tags)** — **healthy, verified.** `snapshot-2026-08-09` exists; tags continuous 08-05 → 08-09, older ones pruned by retention as designed.
- **L3 (Syncthing)** — *"Syncthing service is not running"* in **all 74 runs.** No real-time replication to desktop or phone. Note the counterpoint I owe this: the capture path is Telegram → this agent → `daily/`, which never traverses Syncthing. L3 governs whether the *result* reaches your phone, not whether your message arrives. It is a real defect and a plausible reason the vault feels absent on the phone. It is **not** established as the cause of zero replies.
- **L4 (restic offsite)** — gated on a file outside this session's read scope. **Unverified.**

CLAUDE.md tells you mistakes are reversible because four layers stand behind every write. **That statement is not currently true as written.**

## Zone 7 — The Three Questions

### 1. What did the environment send back?

**From people: nothing.** Six pings, six silences. No inbound file since 07-24. No movement on either open student lead in two weeks. No word written in your hand into this vault since 07-30, and no capture through the channel since 07-05.

**From the machine: one signal, and it is new.** The Loop Review fired at 09:17:01 on the minute the spec names, for the first time in the nine Sundays since you locked the slot. Set against it: a backup check that has failed 74 times out of 74, L3 down for every one of them, and L4 that neither of us can see.

**And one thing the environment did not send back: any evidence of what happened on Monday.** The session that this vault's twelve active projects were built to serve came and went, and the ledger cannot tell you whether it occurred. That is not neglect — it is the architecture. Every artifact routes outside `vault/` by design, and the one in-vault receipt is written by hand.

### 2. What does it change?

**It changes the diagnosis, and I have now had it wrong twice.**

- Through 08-07 I located the fault at your keyboard: nobody writes `due:`, therefore the calendar is empty.
- On 08-08 I corrected that and located it at a dead cron: orders are written only at the Loop Review, and the Loop Review never fires.
- **Today the cron fired, and neither explanation survives.** The ritual works. The channel works. The digest has fired daily without a break. The ping has fired thirty-five times without a break.

What is left, once the mechanical explanations are gone, is narrower and more useful than either: **every loop in this system that requires only the machine is running perfectly, and every loop that requires one line from you is at zero.** Not most. All of them. Six pings, zero replies. Twenty-three sweeps, zero `due:`. Thirty-five evenings, zero numbers. One receipt owed to two children, six nights unwritten.

The design criterion in [[emissary-maintenance]] is *"it must run even if Idi does nothing today."* **The machine half passes that test completely. The contract half — 15 minutes a day — has never been tested, because it has never been run.** And the single counter-example is instructive: the one order that ever closed, closed because you said six words on 07-05 and I wrote the frontmatter. No calendar, no `due:`, no file opened. **The channel that has ever worked is you talking and me writing.**

Your own words from 07-30 name the mechanism: *"move as much work as possible as early as possible so that when the time comes to hand it in, the work is already done."* You did that. The cheatsheet was exported the night before. What the doctrine does not cover is the ten seconds *after* — and that is precisely where every zero in this packet sits.

### 3. What are next week's orders?

**Yours to write. This is the only place they get written, and this is the first time in nine weeks that the place has actually opened.**

Mechanics: one order = one note with `due: YYYY-MM-DD` + a status enum value. It then appears in `bases/calendar.base` and in every morning digest automatically. Dictate them here or dump them dated into `inbox/`; I carve them.

Candidates, ranked by cost — the first three are seconds, not minutes:

1. **The deletion date.** One sentence into [[tutoring-sisters-9-12]]. Approximate-and-marked beats blank. Six nights past, owed to two children. **Highest value in this packet by a distance.** Or say the date out loud and I write the line.
2. **The duplicate-cron word.** One sentence confirming the three prompts are live, so I delete the interim harness jobs before anything starts arriving twice on a channel now proven to fire.
3. **Tomorrow's collision.** Is there a 09:00 sisters session? One word puts `due: 2026-08-10` on the right notes and resolves it; without it, tomorrow is two commitments and no times.
4. **One evening reply tonight.** Three numbers. Seeds the first data this ledger has ever held, and ends a thirty-five-day null.
5. **The cheatsheet's status** — session-two document, or `done`.
6. **Restic** — `env` + `init`. Your hand only; L4 stays dark until then.
7. **The 118-day orphan** — route or delete.
8. **Candidate #1** — type it when it is ripe, never on schedule.

**One structural decision I am putting to you rather than deciding.** Twenty-three empty calendar sweeps and five defects that have survived fourteen daily restatements are strong evidence that the daily digest does not cause change. The 07-05 sitting produced six candidates and one closure, and the one that closed came from a spoken word, not a written `due:`. **Either orders start getting written here, or the calendar and the Orders section should leave the daily spec and this sitting becomes the whole instrument.** Carrying an instrument nobody feeds is how a system starts manufacturing signal about itself. One word decides it; the write is inside my scope, the decision is not.

## Audit

- **Assumptions checked.** Nothing inherited from any prior digest. Re-verified against the filesystem this morning: the `due:` sweep across all five syntaxes vault-wide, all inbox mtimes, `git log` and per-file history, `git tag`, the four agent logs, `backup-health.log` line counts (74/74/0), all four daily notes' frontmatter, the sisters-note mtime, the a-note frontmatter, and the loop-review prompt file byte-compared against the prompt I was given.
- **Correction, and it is the one that matters.** Yesterday I wrote that the Loop Review "is dead" and that the cron was plausibly never installed. It fired today on the specified minute. I had converted eight observations of silence into a claim about a mechanism I could not inspect — a prediction wearing the clothes of a finding. This morning's digest caught the same error mid-flight and refused to pre-report; that instinct was right and I should have had it a day earlier.
- **Second correction, method not fact.** For three weeks the daily digest escalated prose at an unanswered channel. That is the same unfed-loop failure I diagnose elsewhere, performed by me. This packet states each item once.
- **Counterpoint I owe section 3.** The tidy reading of seven silent days is disengagement. I do not have that and the evidence argues against it: the 08-02 export was 45 minutes of real work, and the 07-30 Whiteboard block is twelve numbered points of dense original thinking. **The failure is located precisely at recording what already happened, not at doing it.** Systems that lower capture cost are on-target; systems that prompt for engagement are not. That distinction should survive this sitting.
- **Gap Scan.** Whether the loop-review cron ran and failed on the prior eight Sundays, or was installed recently, is unresolvable from here — `crontab -l` needs an approval this session lacks. L4 is out of read scope. Whether Monday's session happened is unknowable from inside `vault/` by design. Telegram history is invisible to me. **I am reporting on a week whose primary evidence is systematically out of view, and that is structural, not incidental.**
- **Divergence.** The untried inversion, stated once: stop routing capture toward the vault. Let the receipt, the numbers, and the orders arrive as Telegram replies and let me do the writing. I have write access to `projects/` and `daily/`; the only thing I lack is the content. **The one order that ever closed in this vault's history closed exactly this way.** That is now an observation with a precedent behind it, not a proposal.
- **Nothing ambiguous was acted on.** No `due:` field was added to any note, including the two I could most easily justify. The unresolvable crontab, the unverifiable L4, the missing receipt, the stale `.html` path, the absent HTML frontmatter, the `Cash/` enum pollution, the missing tracker instances, the cheat sheet's stale date and status, and tomorrow's undated collision are all reported and all untouched.
- **Nothing fabricated.** No daily note was backdated into existence to receive sleep or energy values that were never recorded. Section 3 quotes out-of-window text and says so in the first line rather than presenting ten-day-old words as this week's.
- **Environmental, unrelated to this task.** Three claude.ai connectors (Gmail, Google Calendar, Google Drive) surfaced unauthorized; they require authorization in claude.ai connector settings and cannot be authorized from a non-interactive session. Nothing here depended on them.
- **Writes this run:** `daily/digests/2026-08-09-loop-review.md` only, plus the compact version to Telegram. No note outside `daily/` was touched, no frontmatter modified, nothing deleted, nothing routed out of `inbox/`, no atomic note touched.
